message:

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds on record.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I'll list the orders to confirm each refund fits against its order amount and to identify the customers to pay.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is below its order amount (161: 6723 of 7280; 163: 12727 of 19145). Customers are acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net of 46023 matches my own check: orders 39605 + 19145 = 58750, less refund 163 of 12727 = 46023, so Alpha's refund for order 163 is reflected correctly. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 4970 matches my check: orders 7280 + 4413 = 11693, less refund 161 of 6723 = 4970. Refund 161 is reflected correctly. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll confirm its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 35816 matches my check: orders 33787 + 2029 = 35816, with no refunds. All three net balances agree with the ledger, and Alpha's refunds are reflected correctly, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 4970, which I already verified against the orders and refund 161.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt's net of 35816 was already verified against its orders with no refunds, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched its verified net balance, so the batch is complete.
